dutch.title: Test van de vertaalmodule
dutch.markdown: Veertig jaar geleden leek de toekomst om de hoek... en het voertuig dat ons zou brengen... was NASA's Space Shuttle. Oorspronkelijk gezien als onderdeel van een groter geïntegreerd [ruimtetransportsysteem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Transportation_System), werd de shuttle gefactureerd als een volledig herbruikbaar voertuig, geheel anders dan de één-en-done capsules van het vervagende Apollo-tijdperk, in staat om maandelijkse (en misschien zelfs wekelijkse) veervluchten naar een lage baan op aarde te maken.

german.title: Test of the translation module
german.markdown: Forty years ago, the future seemed just around the corner—and the vehicle that was going to take us there was NASA’s Space Shuttle. Originally envisioned as part of a larger integrated [space transportation system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Transportation_System), the shuttle was billed as a fully reusable vehicle, totally unlike the one-and-done capsules of the fading Apollo era, capable of making monthly (and perhaps even weekly) ferry flights to low Earth orbit.

runs.initial_markdown: # catinclude Source: https://zotonicwww2.test:8443/en/docs/13301/catinclude URI: https://zotonicwww2.test:8443/id/13301 Language: en ::: {.aside} See also tag#all_catinclude, which is useful to include multiple templates. ::: Include another template based on the category of a resource. The include tag is replaced with the contents of the included template file. You can give arguments to the included template, they will be assigned as variables in the context of the included template. Example: ```erlang {% catinclude "hello.tpl" id %} ``` Assuming that the resource whose id is the value of the template variable id, and that the unique name property of the resource is `my_page_name` is a news article then catinclude will consider the following templates: ```erlang hello.name.my_page_name.tpl hello.news.tpl hello.article.tpl hello.text.tpl hello.tpl ``` This because news is a subcategory of article, which is a subcategory of text. When one of the previous templates is not found then the base template hello.tpl is tried. The catinclude tag will only include the first file it finds, and stops after having found a file to include. If the resource has a unique name (the name property is set), this property is also considered for the catinclude lookup, before the category-based template names. If the resource has name set to foobar, it will first look for `hello.name.foobar.tpl`, then for `hello.news.tpl`, etc. The tag accepts extra arguments, which will be passed as template variables to the included template. The inclusion is always done at runtime, because the selected template depends on the category of the referenced resource. The resource id will be available in the included template as the variable `id`. Instead of passing an id, you can also pass in a list of category names which are to be search for. These names need to be atoms or strings, for example: ```erlang {% catinclude "hello.tpl" [`text`, `article`] %} ``` This will search for the following templates, in order: ```erlang hello.article.tpl hello.text.tpl hello.tpl ``` ::: {.note title="Note"} The search order is reversed from the list order; add the *most specific selector last*. ::: See the tag#include for caching options and argument handling.
